content.comment_body: I mistakenly installed [version_no] and would like to revert back to [version_no], where Czech language was available.

Hello [user_name], Upon installing [version_no], the previous version remains installed. To confirm, check either: 1. Control panel under Programs and Resources to see both versions. 2. Windows Explorer in Program Files under [company_name] to find both. You will see an executable for [product_name], and you can create shortcuts for each. You can use either version; I have the older one in a certain language, and [version_no] in English. Feel free to ask if you need more details. Regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], I'm not certain if uninstalling [version_no] and reinstalling [version_no] will work, since there may be leftover registry entries. From my experience, copying the [product_name] files (entire directory) without installation works. If needed, I can send you the [product_name] [version_no] files in Czech via email.

Alternatively, you can uninstall both versions and then perform separate installations. After uninstalling, install [product_name] [version_no] and download its update, selecting a separate installation path. This lets you use both [version_no] and [version_no] simultaneously, and you can install the Czech language pack with [version_no].
Thanks everyone. I have reinstalled both versions.
Hi, I have [product_name] [version_no]. Is it possible to upgrade this to [version_no] for Czech language support, or do I need to purchase the [version_no] version separately?
No, downgrading from [version_no] to [version_no] is not possible.

You might try the following, though results aren't guaranteed: 1. Download the demo of [product_name] [version_no] from [company_name]. 2. Install it anywhere. 3. Access its installation directory. 4. Copy the file 'Language_cz_CZ.properties' (if included in the demo). 5. Paste this file into your [version_no] directory. 6. Select CZ in the language options. This could work, but note that changes between [version_no] and [version_no] may be missing. You can compare language files between versions using an editor. Always back up or rename files before overwriting, in case something goes wrong. Regards, [user_name]

I tested the 'Czech' language update for [version_no] from the [company_name] website. Some menu items will remain in English if not present in the [product_name] [version_no] language file, for example, specific converter blocks. These features did not exist in [version_no], so appear in English; related help sections won’t display either. Here’s one method: 1. Download the Czech language file for [product_name] [version_no] (e.g., 'czech_v8.luf'). 2. Change the file extension from .luf to .zip and extract it. You’ll get two files and a folder: - module info.dat (not needed), - Language_cs_CZ.properties, - Help folder. 3. Move 'Language_cs_CZ.properties' to the [product_name] [version_no] installation directory. 4. Move 'Help_cs_CZ.jar' from the help folder to the appropriate help directory within [product_name] [version_no]. 5. Back up the 'Language.properties' file, open it with an editor, and add 'language.cs_CZ = Czech' to the language section. Save, then restart [product_name] [version_no], and Czech should be selectable under language options.
Hi, I can't download the 'czech_v8.luf' file—could you please provide a new link? I would like the Czech language files. Thank you.

Hello, You're correct, not all language files are available for download. In the link to my cloud, you’ll find the needed files: - Language_cs_CZ.properties - Help_cs_CZ.jar You can download them here: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced difficulties with language availability and managing different versions of [product_name]. There is frustration over the lack of Czech support in [version_no] and that direct downgrading is impossible. Users discovered that older and newer versions can coexist, but restoring Czech language in the newer version requires unofficial solutions and file modification. Version upgrades have created challenges for those needing specific language support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek simple version management and consistent Czech language support across updates, wishing to restore or maintain Czech functionality without resorting to complex, manual procedures.
